title: Karpathy's List
authors: Talks, code and essays by Andrej Karpathy
summary: The reading list that circulates under Andrej Karpathy's name is a listicle with nothing behind it. What he has actually published is better: a from-scratch course, four essays, and an hour-long talk that cites more than thirty works. Thirty-two entries — his own artifacts and the papers he genuinely put on screen — regrouped into seven chapters, each with the mechanism explained and an honest note on what did not survive.

title: Weng's Guide
summary: Lil'Log is the closest thing applied reinforcement learning and alignment have to a textbook, but it is a blog: sixty-odd posts in reverse-chronological order with no path through them. Twenty of them, chosen and ordered into a route that runs from policy gradients to reward hacking to self-improving agent harnesses. The curation is mine; the work being read is hers.

title: Sutskever's List
authors: Reading list attributed to Ilya Sutskever
summary: The ~30 works Ilya Sutskever reportedly handed John Carmack, with the line "if you really learn all of these, you'll know 90% of what matters today". The provenance is contested; the syllabus is excellent either way. Twenty-seven works, regrouped into five chapters that follow the argument, each with the mechanism explained and an honest note on what did not survive.

title: Deep Learning
iconAlt: Cover of Deep Learning by Goodfellow, Bengio and Courville
summary: The standard graduate reference for the field, in three parts: the applied mathematics and machine-learning background, the deep networks themselves, and the research frontier of generative and probabilistic models. These are my section-by-section notes as I work through it.
